claims.name: Toy.clamp_spec
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Returns Toy.Lifted.module "clamp" [FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.summary: The exported clamp function returns the input bounded by the supplied limits using signed 32-bit comparisons.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit bit-vector inputs: the value, lower limit, and upper limit.
Comparisons read the bit patterns as signed 32-bit integers. The result is one of the original inputs, so this claim introduces no arithmetic wraparound.
Returns requires an execution that terminates without a trap and produces exactly the selected input.
caveats: The claim does not require the lower limit to be less than or equal to the upper limit; when limits are reversed, the stated nested comparisons still determine the result.
It does not specify behavior for calls with other argument types or counts.
claims.reason: The statement covers every 32-bit input triple and returns `lo` below the lower bound, `hi` above the upper bound, and `x` otherwise, using signed comparisons. This matches the stated rule, including when the limits are reversed (as in the example returning 2).

claims.name: Toy.gcd_spec
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints terminates with the greatest common divisor.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Returns Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.summary: The exported gcd function returns the unsigned greatest common divisor of its two 32-bit inputs.
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit-vector inputs, interpreted as unsigned natural numbers for the greatest-common-divisor calculation.
The result is the 32-bit representation of that natural-number gcd; it fits without wraparound because it is no larger than either input.
Returns requires an execution that terminates without a trap and produces exactly the specified result.
caveats: The claim does not use signed interpretations of the inputs; bit patterns that might be viewed as negative are treated as unsigned.
It does not specify behavior for calls with other argument types or counts.
claims.reason: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the statement specifies their unsigned natural-number gcd represented as a 32-bit value. That matches the intent.

claims.name: Toy.sum_to_spec
claims.summary: The exported sum_to function returns the sum of the natural numbers below the unsigned value of its 32-bit input, reduced to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit bit-vector input, read as an unsigned natural number.
The specified sum adds the values from zero up to but excluding the input; the final natural-number sum is converted to 32 bits, so larger sums wrap modulo 2 to the 32nd power.
Returns requires an execution that terminates without a trap and produces exactly that 32-bit result.
caveats: Inputs whose top bit is set are large unsigned values, not negative numbers; the claim still quantifies over them, though it does not guarantee practical execution time beyond requiring a terminating execution.
The mathematical sum is defined recursively and does not itself wrap; only its conversion to 32 bits does.
It does not specify behavior for calls with other argument types or counts.
claims.reason: For every 32-bit input, the statement sums the natural numbers below its unsigned value and converts the result to 32 bits, matching the intended wrapped sum.
